title: Anthropic Signs $45 Billion Compute Deal With British Startup Nscale
excerpt: The six-year agreement for Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin chips at a West Virginia data center marks Anthropic's largest single compute commitment as AI firms race to lock in infrastructure.
body:
• Anthropic has signed an approximately $45 billion, six-year deal to rent compute from Nscale, a British AI infrastructure company founded in 2024.
  • The agreement covers Nvidia's Vera Rubin chips at a West Virginia data center, with compute deliveries starting late 2027.
  • Anthropic's total compute commitments over the past eight months now span deals with Nscale, Volta, AMD, SpaceX, Amazon, and Google/Broadcom.
  • The spending spree positions Anthropic to compete directly with OpenAI for leadership in frontier AI model development.

Anthropic's Largest Single Compute Bet

Anthropic has signed a deal worth approximately $45 billion to rent computing power from Nscale, a British AI infrastructure company founded in 2024, according to a report first published by Bloomberg. The six-year agreement will supply Anthropic with Nvidia's Vera Rubin chips — a state-of-the-art architecture that coordinates six different chip types working in concert.

Compute deliveries will come from a data center in West Virginia, with capacity expected to come online starting in late 2027. Nscale, which has also signed infrastructure deals with Microsoft, is positioning itself as a major independent compute provider for AI companies that need capacity beyond what hyperscalers allocate.

The deal is Anthropic's single largest compute commitment and signals the company's determination to match OpenAI in raw training and inference capacity.

A Spending Spree Without Precedent

The Nscale agreement is part of an extraordinary eight-month run in which Anthropic has locked in computing resources across multiple providers and geographies:

In early 2026, the company signed a $10 billion, six-year agreement with Volta for compute from a data center in Norway. In July, it committed $5 billion to AMD. A deal with SpaceX now provides $1.25 billion per month in compute from two data centers. In April, Anthropic secured an additional 5 gigawatts of compute capacity from Amazon and expanded its arrangement with Google and Broadcom.

Taken together, the commitments represent one of the most aggressive infrastructure buildouts by any private technology company. The total spend dwarfs what most publicly traded tech firms allocate to capital expenditure.

The Race for AI Supremacy

Anthropic's compute accumulation reflects a core belief shared across the AI industry: the companies that control the most computing power will build the most capable models, and the most capable models will capture the most revenue.

OpenAI, Anthropic's primary competitor, has pursued a similar strategy, raising billions in capital and negotiating its own infrastructure deals. Google, Meta, and Amazon are building out their own AI capacity while also serving as compute suppliers to startups.

For Anthropic, the challenge extends beyond procurement. The company must convert raw compute into models that justify the investment — a bet that assumes continued demand for AI capabilities from enterprise and consumer markets. The Vera Rubin chips Anthropic is renting represent Nvidia's next architectural leap, and their performance at scale remains unproven in production environments.

Nscale's Rapid Ascent

The deal also highlights the emergence of independent infrastructure companies like Nscale, which was founded just two years ago and has already secured contracts with two of the most prominent names in AI. By offering compute capacity without the platform lock-in of hyperscale cloud providers, companies like Nscale and Volta have carved out a niche in the AI supply chain.

Whether the current pace of AI infrastructure investment is sustainable remains an open question. But for now, Anthropic is making clear that it intends to compete at the frontier — and is willing to spend at a scale that would have been unimaginable in the industry even two years ago.
